houston.claimAsFiled: City of Houston (geoid 4835000) has no Euclidean zoning; deed-restriction / no-zoning regime. Do not invent a zoning layer. [status SEARCHED-AND-ABSENT]
whatHoustonActuallyRegulates: Special Minimum Lot Size areas (Ch.42) - 722 polygons, 236 distinct LOTSIZE values 2176-55648 sq ft, each ordinance-cited, with SFR_Restriction flag and expiration dates
Special Minimum Building Lines (Ch.42) - 195 polygons, 30 distinct setback values 10-100 ft, ordinance-cited
Historic Districts (City of Houston) - 23 polygons; certificate-of-appropriateness regime
Heritage Districts, Green Corridor, Major Activity Center (8), Market Based Parking (1), Walkable Places / TOD / Transit Corridor Streets and Parcels
Restricted Lot Driveway Access + Schools Primary Entrance (Ch.42 platting constraints)
Prohibited Yard Parking Applications; Street Width Exception areas
Municipally-enforced deed restrictions (enforced by Legal Dept; not published as a single GIS layer)

layersFound.name: Special Minimum Lot Size
layersFound.whatItCarries: Hard minimum lot area in sq ft binding subdivision/replat of the covered blockface. Directly answers 'can this lot be subdivided / what is the smallest lot permitted here'.

layersFound.name: Special Minimum Building Lines
layersFound.whatItCarries: Mandatory front setback in feet, ordinance-cited. Directly constrains the buildable envelope.

layersFound.name: Historic Districts (City of Houston)
layersFound.whatItCarries: Certificate of Appropriateness required; constrains demolition and exterior alteration.

layersFound.name: Houston Land Use (Grouped)
layersFound.whatItCarries: Observed land use, NOT regulatory. Must never be served as zoning.

falseAbsenceRate.strictDefinition: LAYER_FOUND only (a queryable municipal zoning polygon layer Z1 should have found)
falseAbsenceRate.misclassifiedDefinition: LAYER_FOUND + REGULATION_EXISTS_NON_GIS - rows where SEARCHED-AND-ABSENT is the wrong status even when no layer is recoverable
falseAbsenceRate.note: Sample was deliberately biased toward the cities MOST likely to have zoning (largest first). The true rate over all 105 is likely LOWER than this sample for LAYER_FOUND and HIGHER for REGULATION_EXISTS_NON_GIS, since the long tail is tiny towns that plausibly have an ordinance but no GIS.

probeMethodDefects.defect: Houston hardcoded to SEARCHED-AND-ABSENT before any network call
probeMethodDefects.evidence: z1_houston_probe.py probe_city(): if city_key == 'houston-tx': return {... 'status':'SEARCHED-AND-ABSENT', 'probes':[{'kind':'doctrine','result':'absent-no-euclidean-zoning'}]}. The status word SEARCHED is factually untrue for this row; a doctrine assertion was laundered into a probe finding, then re-reported downstream as a market signal.
probeMethodDefects.fix: Never let a belief write a status that means 'we looked'. Doctrine rows need their own status and must still probe.

probeMethodDefects.defect: ArcGIS Server folder recursion missing - root-only enumeration
probeMethodDefects.evidence: Z1 logged {'kind':'municipal-root','url':'https://gis.deerparktx.gov/arcgis/rest/services','services':[]} while that root live-returns folders ['Hosted','Utilities','WGS84'] plus 10 services. find_zoning_in_services_root() reads only the top-level services array. Deer Park's zoning is one level down at WGS84/Zoning_WGS84. This single defect produced the only confirmed false absence in the sample and recurs on every ArcGIS Server organised by folder.
probeMethodDefects.fix: Recurse the folders[] array one to two levels before declaring a host empty.

probeMethodDefects.defect: AGOL discovery is title-gated, so it can only find layers already named for the city
probeMethodDefects.evidence: agol_search() drops any result failing ZONING_TITLE_RE, then name_matches() drops any whose title/owner/snippet lacks the city name. A correctly-published layer titled e.g. 'Current Zoning (Public View)' under a municipal org is invisible unless the org is already known. 84 of 104 non-Houston absences rest on an AGOL search that returned hits:0.
probeMethodDefects.fix: On any hit, extract the orgId from the service URL and enumerate that org's /arcgis/rest/services. Org enumeration is how Houston's 291 services were found in one call.

probeMethodDefects.defect: municipal_roots() is hostname guesswork with a 0-for-104 success rate
probeMethodDefects.evidence: Across all 104 non-Houston absences the municipal-root path returned services:[] every single time. The synthetic pattern gis.<slug>tx.gov resolves DNS almost nowhere (verified DNS-fail: gis.leaguecitytx.gov, gis.texascitytx.gov, gis.laporte-tx.gov, maps.humbletx.gov). A control that never fires is not evidence of absence - it is a no-op wearing the costume of a probe.
probeMethodDefects.fix: Discover the host from the city's own site / Hub domain instead of guessing; treat DNS failure as NOT-PROBED, never as evidence.

probeMethodDefects.defect: Dead or broken hosts are recorded identically to genuine absence
probeMethodDefects.evidence: Webster's advertised zoning host http://www1.cityofwebster.com/arcgis/rest/services returns an Esri 'Application Error' page; Z1 logged services:[] - indistinguishable from a city that never published. Same for HTTP 500 at maps.cityofconroe.org.
probeMethodDefects.fix: Record HTTP status and body class; a 500 or DNS failure is an infrastructure state, not a data finding.

probeMethodDefects.defect: 105 absences collapsed to one boilerplate reason string; only 13 sampled into the close artifact
probeMethodDefects.evidence: Every non-Houston absence carries a byte-identical reason. The close artifact shipped searchedAndAbsentSample of 13 rows for 105 absences, so a reviewer reading only the artifact cannot tell a well-probed absence from a hits:0 no-op. Full per-city evidence survived only because P:/tmp/z1_houston_probe_log.json was left on disk.
probeMethodDefects.fix: Per-row reason must record what was actually tried and what came back.

absenceTaxonomyProposed.meaning: Unincorporated territory; no municipal zoning power exists (TX counties generally cannot zone).
absenceTaxonomyProposed.productBehaviour: Answer affirmatively: 'no municipal zoning applies here'. A POSITIVE fact, safe to serve. Fall through to county/state constraints.

absenceTaxonomyProposed.meaning: Authority exists and regulates development, but not via mapped use-districts. Houston is the type specimen.
absenceTaxonomyProposed.productBehaviour: Serve the Ch.42-class constraint layers (min lot size, building lines, historic/conservation, parking). NEVER say 'no zoning' bare - that reads as unconstrained and is affirmatively misleading to a buyer.

absenceTaxonomyProposed.meaning: A zoning ordinance demonstrably exists but is published only as PDF/tile/paper.
absenceTaxonomyProposed.productBehaviour: Honest absence WITH the ordinance citation and link; explicitly 'zoning exists, not machine-readable'. Eligible for the acquisition backlog.

absenceTaxonomyProposed.meaning: A layer exists but is behind auth/token/paywall.
absenceTaxonomyProposed.productBehaviour: Do not serve. Route to acquisition. Must never be reported as a data gap - it is an access gap.

absenceTaxonomyProposed.meaning: A layer is advertised but its server errors, DNS-fails, or 500s (Webster, Conroe).
absenceTaxonomyProposed.productBehaviour: Retry on a schedule; treat as transient. Never counts as evidence of absence.

absenceTaxonomyProposed.meaning: RESERVED for: a real search path executed, returned a live 200, and no zoning layer exists. Requires naming the paths tried.
Search returned nothing and we cannot distinguish absence from probe failure (e.g. AGOL hits:0 plus a DNS-failed host guess).
absenceTaxonomyProposed.productBehaviour: Honest absence, LOW confidence, flagged for re-probe. This is where most of Z1's 105 actually belong.

cp1.houstonPrediction: PARTLY_TRUE_BUT_WRONG_FOR_PRODUCT. Houston genuinely has no Euclidean zoning districts, so 'no zoning district layer' is defensible as a literal statement. But Houston publishes extensive Chapter 42 / building-line / special-district GIS on an open-data portal, and the product question 'what can I build here' IS answerable. Registry status must change from SEARCHED-AND-ABSENT to a no-euclidean-districts-but-regulated status.
cp1.houstonMethodPrediction: Z1 short-circuited houston-tx on doctrine before any network call (confirmed by reading probe source: probe_city returns early with probes=[{kind:doctrine}]). So the claim is an ASSERTION, not a finding.

falseAbsenceRatePrediction.rationale: Z1's absence path is AGOL title-match + a municipal-host guess list. Cities whose GIS is on a county/regional host, a differently-named AGOL org, or an unguessed hostname will read absent. Expect incorporated cities >20k to be the worst hit.

cp1.expectedDominantDefect: AGOL name_matches gating rejects hits whose title lacks the city name (e.g. county-hosted or regional layers), and municipal_roots is a fixed hostname-guess list.

cp2.houstonDetail: Predicted PARTLY_TRUE_BUT_WRONG_FOR_PRODUCT and that Z1 short-circuited before probing. Both confirmed: the doctrine short-circuit is in the source, and Houston publishes parcel-precise Ch.42 lot-size/setback polygons that answer the buildability question.
cp2.falseAbsenceDetail: Pre-registered 25% (band 15-45) for LAYER_FOUND. Actual strict false-absence rate 4.8% (1 of 21), on a sample deliberately biased toward the likeliest cities. My pre-registered suspect (AGOL name-gating) was NOT the main producer of recoverable layers; the one real recovery came from a different defect (folder recursion). Matches the standing pattern that the obvious suspect is usually the wrong one.
cp2.netVerdict: Z1's DATA finding is largely sound - Houston MSA municipalities genuinely do not publish much zoning GIS. Z1's METHOD and STATUS VOCABULARY are not. Damage is concentrated in Houston (an unprobed assertion) and in the 84 no-signal rows that claim 'searched' on the strength of a control that never fired.

adversarialFindings: I tried hardest to break Z1 on League City and Pasadena, the two most suspicious rejects, and Z1 WAS RIGHT on both: the League City hit is Dickinson's service (PIP=0 at League City centroid, extent caps at 29.482) and both Pasadena hits are Pasadena CALIFORNIA (extent -118.2/34.1). Reporting these as false absences would have traded one wrong answer for another.

MY OWN first-pass automated resample fell into the exact trap this dispatch exists to catch: it flagged LAYER_FOUND for 7 of 7 cities because service names matched /zon/ - they were hurricane evacuation zones, USFS seed zones, federal fire initial-attack zones and rail blast zones. Only after adding a noise filter AND point-in-polygon verification did the rate collapse to 1. A name-matching probe manufactures presence exactly as easily as it manufactures absence.

The one confirmed recovery (Deer Park) was found BY HAND, not by my automated pass - my own org-enumeration script also missed it, because Deer Park's layer sits on a self-hosted ArcGIS Server with no AGOL presence. My method therefore shares a blind spot with Z1's: both are AGOL-centric. The true false-absence rate over all 105 is likely HIGHER than the 4.8% measured.

WHAT MY METHOD CANNOT SEE: self-hosted ArcGIS/Geoserver behind unguessable hostnames; zoning published only as PDF/tile/paper (I made no attempt to enumerate ordinances, so REGULATION_EXISTS_NON_GIS is almost certainly undercounted - I can confirm it only where a broken service advertised itself); auth-walled layers; and any city whose GIS sits on a county host I did not enumerate.

Sampling bias is deliberate and one-directional: I picked the largest and most-likely-zoned cities first, so 4.8% is an UPPER bound for LAYER_FOUND on this sample shape and says little about the 84-city long tail.

The H1-seam concern is NOT confirmed by this lane's evidence: the seam's cityKey scoping is sound and the Deer Park recovery would slot into it cleanly (its SF1/GC codes collide by name across cities, which is exactly what cityKey scoping exists to handle). The Factory 1.5 risk found here is upstream of the seam - in DISCOVERY, not in the payload contract.

Unfalsifiable-control pattern: same defect class as the special-district writer's vacuous verify and the bypassed warm preflight gate - a control that structurally cannot fail (municipal_roots 0-for-104; the Houston doctrine short-circuit) counted as evidence that it passed.
